title: Authorship Cluster: Survey on Hallucination in Large Language Models
summary: This community centers on the 2023 survey paper 'A Survey on Hallucination in Large Language Models: Principles, Taxonomy, Challenges, and Open Questions' and its eleven authors. The cluster is defined entirely by the 'AUTHORED_BY' relationships linking the paper to individuals such as Lei Huang, Bing Qin, and Ting Liu. It represents a collaborative academic effort to systematically categorize and analyze hallucination phenomena in LLMs.
key_findings: The core entity is a 2023 arXiv paper (arXiv:2311.05232) focused on the principles, taxonomy, and challenges of hallucination in Large Language Models.
The paper has a large authorship team consisting of eleven researchers, including Lei Huang, Weijiang Yu, Weitao Ma, and Weihong Zhong.
Senior researchers Bing Qin and Ting Liu are listed as co-authors, indicating a collaborative effort likely spanning multiple research groups.
The community structure is strictly bipartite, connecting the single paper entity to its human authors without internal relationships between the authors themselves in this dataset.
The paper is cited in the context of other works on retrieval-augmented generation and knowledge graph reasoning, suggesting its relevance to broader NLP challenges.
